scams.name: Berlin 'Speak English?' Opener & Alexanderplatz Pickpocket Team
scams.description: r/berlin 'Excuse me....Speak English?' (2025) is a 2025 report on Berlin's most common approach-scam opener. A stranger — typically working with 2–3 accomplices — approaches tourists with 'Excuse me, do you speak English?' to initiate a conversation that distracts from a second team member lifting your phone, wallet, or camera from an unzipped bag. r/berlinsocialclub 'Almost got pickpocketed in Alexanderplatz' (2024) and r/Scams '(Germany) Almost got scammed in Berlin, and gave away' (2025) document the 2025 continuation. Variants: (1) 'charity clipboard' signing distraction; (2) map unfolded over your bag asking for directions; (3) 'bracelet gift' placed on wrist followed by payment demand; (4) 'I need €20 for train to Poland — emergency' sob story. For older travelers in Berlin, the defensive playbook: (1) keep wallet in a front pocket or money belt; never in a backpack's top compartment; (2) a firm 'no thank you' (or the German 'Nein, danke') and keep walking — do not engage in conversation; (3) if approached by a 'charity' clipboard, refuse to sign anything; (4) in crowded tourist zones (Alexanderplatz, Brandenburger Tor, Museum Island), keep your hand on your bag; (5) r/askberliners 'Any other scams I should know about?' (2025) is the 2025 Berliner-crowdsourced scam primer; (6) report theft to Berlin Polizei non-emergency (110 is emergency; 030-4664-4664 is non-emergency) and file a written report (Strafanzeige) at any Polizeiabschnitt — required for travel insurance claims.
scams.avoidance: Keep wallet in front pocket or money belt — never in backpack top Firm 'Nein, danke' + keep walking — no conversation Refuse ALL clipboard signing requests Keep hand on bag in crowded tourist zones Report theft: Polizei non-emergency 030-4664-4664; file Strafanzeige
scams.location: Alexanderplatz, Brandenburger Tor, Potsdamer Platz, Museum Island, Hackescher Markt, Kurfürstendamm, S-Bahn/U-Bahn platforms citywide

scams.name: Fake S-Bahn / U-Bahn Ticket Inspector Cash Fine Scam
scams.description: r/berlin 'Just got scammed at the train station by an official worker (?)' (2025) is a 2025 report and r/berlin 'on the sbahn did i witness a scam, or the rudest group of ticket inspectors' (2025) is a companion. r/askberliners 'New scam Ostkreuz / BER Airport / South Europeans targeted' (2025) documents the specific Ostkreuz/BER variant. The pattern: individuals in plain clothes or fake uniforms claim to be ticket inspectors (Fahrscheinkontrolleure) after checking your ticket; they assert your ticket is 'invalid' (wrong zone, wrong validation, wrong date) and demand a €60 'on-the-spot fine' in cash. Real BVG/S-Bahn inspectors: (1) work in teams of 2–3, always with a photo ID badge (Dienstausweis) clearly displayed; (2) the official fine is €60, paid either immediately with a printed receipt OR within 2 weeks via bank transfer to the BVG address on the printed ticket; (3) they NEVER demand cash without giving you a printed notice. For older travelers using Berlin public transit, the defensive playbook: (1) buy tickets from BVG automats or the BVG app (Fahrinfo or 'BVG Fahrinfo Plus') — cover Zones A/B/C; (2) VALIDATE (entwerten) your single-ride ticket at the yellow/red machine on the platform BEFORE boarding — an un-validated single ticket is functionally a fare dodge (€60 fine); (3) if an 'inspector' demands cash, DEMAND to see their Dienstausweis photo ID; refuse to pay cash; ask for a printed fine notice (Erhöhtes Beförderungsentgelt) with the BVG payment details; (4) if a genuine fine is issued, you have 2 weeks to pay via bank transfer via BVG — no cash needed; (5) r/berlin 'How do you tell the fake transport police from the real ones?' (2022) documents older confirmation; (6) BVG customer service: 030-19449.
scams.avoidance: DEMAND to see Dienstausweis (photo ID badge) from any 'inspector' Refuse cash demands — genuine fines allow 2-week bank transfer VALIDATE (entwerten) single tickets at yellow/red platform machines BEFORE boarding Buy tickets only via BVG automats or 'BVG Fahrinfo Plus' app If genuine fine issued, pay via bank transfer to BVG — NEVER cash to individual
scams.location: S-Bahn platforms (Alexanderplatz, Friedrichstraße, Hauptbahnhof, Ostkreuz), U-Bahn platforms citywide, BVG regional trains

scams.name: Brandenburger Tor Petition & Bracelet Pickpocket Distraction
scams.description: r/askberliners 'Any other scams I should know about?' (2025) and r/askberliners 'Was I scammed?' (2025) are the anchors on Berlin's clipboard/bracelet distraction scams. A 'charity worker' (often posing as a deaf-mute petition collector for a disabled-children's cause) approaches with a clipboard, asking for a signature. While you sign, an accomplice lifts your wallet or phone from your bag. Bracelet variant: the 'collector' weaves a fabric friendship bracelet and ties it onto your wrist as a 'gift,' then demands €10–€30 'donation.' Variants include: (1) 'fake deaf' petition claiming EU charity for disabled children; (2) 'friendship bracelet' tied on wrist followed by cash demand; (3) 'photo with costumed character' (Spider-Man, Pikachu near Brandenburger Tor) at €10–€15 'photo fee' disputed afterward; (4) 'rose sellers' who place a rose in your hand then demand €5–€15. For older travelers at Berlin's major tourist squares, the defensive playbook: (1) REFUSE all clipboard signing requests — no legitimate EU charity collects signatures at Brandenburger Tor; (2) REFUSE all 'gift' items placed on your wrist — if a bracelet is tied on, cut it off with scissors later; do NOT pay; (3) costumed characters at Brandenburger Tor / Checkpoint Charlie are not official — if you want a photo, set a price in advance (€2–€5 is fair) or decline; (4) keep hands on bag when approached; (5) r/berlin 'Are beggars always trying to scam?' (2025) is the 2025 community view; (6) genuine Berlin charities collect via bank transfer or registered street collection with visible IDs — never with unofficial clipboards on tourist squares.
scams.avoidance: Refuse ALL clipboard signing — no legit EU charity collects this way at Brandenburger Tor Refuse 'gift' bracelets; cut off if tied on — do NOT pay Set photo price BEFORE costumed character photo (€2–€5 fair) or decline Keep hand on bag in crowded squares Report aggressive solicitation: Polizei 030-4664-4664
scams.location: Brandenburger Tor plaza, Pariser Platz, Museum Island, Gendarmenmarkt, Tiergarten perimeter, Hackescher Markt tourist-strip

scams.name: BER Airport Taxi Overcharge & Unlicensed 'Transfer' Touts
scams.description: r/askberliners 'Taxi From Airport' (2025) is a 2025 report on BER taxi realities. BER is 18 km southeast of central Berlin — legitimate fares: licensed TSB/Taxi Berlin metered taxi €50–€60 to Mitte, €55–€70 to Charlottenburg; Uber and FreeNow via app €35–€55 depending on surge; scam-proof S-Bahn S9/S45 from BER-Flughafen to Alexanderplatz €4.40 (Zones ABC), 30 minutes. r/askberliners 'New scam Ostkreuz / BER Airport / South Europeans targeted' (2025) is a on BER-area scam activity. Scam variants: (1) drivers at the curb or arrivals hall quoting 'flat €120' to Mitte when metered is €50–€60; (2) 'limo' or 'black car' touts quoting €150–€200; (3) unlicensed operators with no meter demanding cash at the end; (4) 'private transfer' online-booked services that disappear with the deposit; (5) taxi driver claiming the meter is 'broken' and demanding €80+ flat rate. For older travelers arriving at BER, the clean playbook: (1) S-Bahn S9 or S45 from BER-Flughafen T1-2 station to Alexanderplatz/Ostkreuz is €4.40 (ABC zone) and takes 30 minutes — the scam-proof default; (2) licensed TSB/Taxi Berlin metered taxi at the official taxi queue: €50–€70 to most central destinations — REFUSE 'flat rate' quotes; (3) Uber/FreeNow via app with fare estimate screenshot: €35–€55 depending on surge; (4) Flughafen-Express 'FEX' train from BER to Berlin Hauptbahnhof is €4.40, 35 minutes — also scam-proof; (5) refuse ANY driver soliciting in the arrivals hall — walk outside to the official taxi queue; (6) if a driver claims the meter is 'broken,' exit and take the next cab; (7) never pay cash beyond the metered amount — ask for a printed Quittung (receipt).
scams.avoidance: S-Bahn S9/S45 from BER T1-2 to Alexanderplatz: €4.40, 30 min — scam-proof Licensed metered TSB/Taxi Berlin at official queue: €50–€70 to center Uber/FreeNow via app with fare screenshot: €35–€55 Flughafen-Express FEX to Hauptbahnhof: €4.40, 35 min REFUSE drivers soliciting in arrivals hall; ask for printed Quittung
scams.location: Berlin Brandenburg Airport (BER) Terminal 1/2 arrivals, airport curb taxi queue, ride-share pickup zones, 'limo' tout solicitation areas

scams.name: Berlin Apartment / STR Rental Scam (Kleinanzeigen Prop-Money & 'CONNY' Digital Trap)
scams.description: r/berlinsocialclub 'got scammed with prop money on Kleinanzeigen' (2025) is a 2025 report on Berlin's Kleinanzeigen apartment-fraud pattern and r/berlinsocialclub 'A Total Nightmare and a "Digital Trap" CONNY' (2025) is a 2025 report on the 'CONNY' fake-tenancy-legal-service scam. r/askberliners 'Got scammed while trying to rent an apartment in Berlin' (2025) documents broader 2025 patterns. Scam variants: (1) Kleinanzeigen 'apartment for rent' listing with photos stolen from real listings — 'landlord' asks for 3 months' rent (€3,000–€6,000) via SEPA transfer sight-unseen; keys never arrive; (2) in-person viewing where 'landlord' shows apartment, takes deposit in cash, then gives keys that don't work (the 'apartment' isn't theirs); (3) 'CONNY' digital-trap — fake 'tenancy-protection service' harvesting bank details; (4) counterfeit 'prop money' paid as deposit; (5) 'short-term Berlin apartment' listings on Facebook Marketplace / Craigslist demanding Zelle/PayPal 'friends and family' (non-refundable). For older travelers booking Berlin accommodation, the defensive playbook: (1) book ONLY through Airbnb, VRBO, or Booking.com platform payment — NEVER Zelle, Venmo, Cash App, PayPal friends-and-family, or SEPA bank transfer to an individual; (2) for long-term Berlin rentals, use ImmobilienScout24, Immowelt, or verified WG-Gesucht listings — NEVER Kleinanzeigen for sight-unseen bookings 'Don't ever allow anyone from kleinanzeigen into your home' (2025); (3) for in-person deposits, pay via bank transfer with a legitimate paper Mietvertrag (rental contract) with the landlord's full legal name + address; (4) AVOID 'CONNY' and similar digital-only tenancy-protection services; (5) legitimate hotels: Hotel Adlon Kempinski, Regent Berlin, Hotel am Steinplatz, 25hours Hotel Bikini Berlin, Hotel Q!; (6) for Berlin rentals at specific Mitte neighborhoods, verify the Handelsregister / Grundbuch ownership via notary before paying any deposit; (7) report fraud: Berlin Polizei Kriminalpolizei (030-4664-4664) + Kleinanzeigen Trust & Safety.
scams.avoidance: Book STRs ONLY via Airbnb/VRBO/Booking.com platform payment Long-term rentals: ImmobilienScout24, Immowelt, verified WG-Gesucht — NOT Kleinanzeigen Pay deposits via bank transfer with legitimate paper Mietvertrag + landlord legal name AVOID 'CONNY' and digital-only tenancy services Verify Grundbuch (land registry) ownership before any deposit
scams.location: Kleinanzeigen (eBay Kleinanzeigen) rental listings, Facebook Marketplace Berlin rentals, Airbnb/Booking.com off-platform solicitations, WG-Gesucht listings

scams.name: Berlin Shell Game, Three-Card Monte & Street Gambling Hustle
scams.description: Berlin's tourist squares host persistent shell-game and three-card monte hustles operated by coordinated teams of 5–8 people. r/askberliners 'Any other scams I should know about?' (2025) and r/askberliners 'Was I scammed?' (2025) reference these 2025 patterns. The setup: (1) a 'dealer' moves 3 shells/cups around hiding a ball or card — a tourist is invited to bet €20–€50 on which shell contains the ball; (2) 'shills' in the crowd pretend to win big (€100+) to lure real marks; (3) once a tourist commits, sleight-of-hand ensures they lose every round; (4) if a tourist protests or tries to leave with winnings, a 'security' shill intimidates them; (5) variant: three-card monte with playing cards; (6) 'bet on which cup has the pea' played at Brandenburger Tor or Museum Island bridges. These are 100% rigged — no amount of 'skill' wins consistently. For older travelers in Berlin, the defensive playbook: (1) NEVER participate in shell-game or three-card monte — ALL are 100% rigged; (2) if you see others 'winning,' they are shills (accomplices) paid by the dealer to lure marks; (3) if you see the setup forming in front of you (circle of people around a folded cardboard table), walk away and warn nearby tourists; (4) German law classifies these as illegal gambling (Glücksspiel) — if asked to participate, refuse and report to Berlin Polizei (030-4664-4664); (5) a common related scam is the 'winning' tourist who suddenly can't leave with their cash — 'security' shills block the exit until winnings are 'forfeited'; (6) if you see this pattern and suspect someone is about to be scammed, a loud 'this is a scam' in English usually breaks up the circle; (7) r/berlin 'Excuse me....Speak English?' (2025) covers the parallel opener-scam that often precedes shell-game steering.
scams.avoidance: NEVER participate — all shell games are 100% rigged Walk away + warn nearby tourists if you see the setup forming Ignore 'winners' in crowd — they are paid shills Shout 'this is a scam' in English to break up the circle Report illegal gambling: Berlin Polizei 030-4664-4664
scams.location: Brandenburger Tor plaza, Alexanderplatz, Museum Island bridges, Unter den Linden, Friedrichstraße pedestrian zone, Hackescher Markt
